To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a baculoviral fibroblast factor (vFGFs) induces matrix metalloproteinase and caspase activation that results in basal lamina degradation and systemic infection.

a baculoviral fibroblast-growth-factor-like protein (vFGF-1) signals a stepwise cascade that culminates in remodeling of basal laminae, which is required for baculovirus infection of the insect tracheal system and for systemic infection.

a baculoviral-encoded fibroblast-like growth factor (vFgf) signals a stepwise cascade of activation wherein matrix metal-loproteases activate effectors caspases, culminating in remodeling of basal laminae lining the tracheal cells and the establishment of efficient baculovirus infections.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating mechanisms of infection of arthropods by viruses that are transmitted by arthropod vectors.
the molecular mechanisms that viruses employ to escape the invertebrate host.
understanding the molecular mechanisms of viral infection of invertebrates and vertebrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

vFGF is a potent enhancer of systemic infection by baculo-viruses and that the vFGFs are a new class of FGFs that are not only involved in developmental processes but also in the pathogenesis of viral infections.
a baculoviral-encoded FGF, by activating protease cascades, mediates a previously unrecognized pathway for the escape of viruses from basal laminae.
vFGF, matrix metalloproteinases, and caspses play a critical role during baculovirus infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the baculovirus vFGF is a master regulator of basal lamina remodeling that enhances baculovirus systemic infection.
a viral FGF, in conjunction with a protease cascade, mediates basal lamina remodeling, thereby enabling systemic infection and transmission.
a baculovirally encoded FGF induces basal lamina remodeling by signaling protease activation, which leads to efficient systemic infection and viral dissemination to other hosts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vFGFs are a new family of viral proteins that are likely to be used in diverse ways during viral infections.
vFGF is the first viral factor that is shown to remodel basal lamina.
a viral protein that mimics the function of a normal host protein can hijack the host's own proteolytic machinery to enhance infection.
